content:
inc-bot: INCIDENT 1872003456 - High error rate and pod crashloops on serving-runtime (autoscale thrash). Paging oncall.
oncall-sre: seeing a burst of 5xx + OOMs across eu-west GPUs, started alert fuzz suppression to avoid paging spam :warning:
sre_lead: @oncall-sre ack, can you post current error sample and recent autoscaler events?
oncall-sre: logs excerpt:
```
[2026-05-10T14:23:01Z] runtime: panic: runtime: out of memory
[2026-05-10T14:23:05Z] cuda: cuCtxCreate failed: out of memory
[2026-05-10T14:23:06Z] kubelet: pod serving-runtime-az4-7fb9 CrashLoopBackOff
```
Also HPA scale events: +12 pods in 2m then -10 in 3m repeating.
runtime-eng: that pattern smells like rapid up/down triggers cache thrash -> OOMs when nodes boot and kernels not warmed. Also saw nv_peer_mem warnings earlier.
ml-infra: models affected: rdx-2b-quant and rdx-4b-q8. The 4b pods show higher memory footprint; quant profiles may be slightly off after the recent kernel update.
prod-support: customers hitting 5xx and rate-limited retries. 2 customers have reported timeouts impacting feeds.
eng-platform: autoscaler logs:
```
2026-05-10T14:22:40 scale-up group gpu-pool desired=22 -> actual=34
2026-05-10T14:24:10 scale-down initiated threshold=2m
2026-05-10T14:25:30 scale-up triggered again desired=40
```
ops-shift: looks like cloud provider is provisioning nodes slower than scheduler expects, causing pods to backoff and then crash when kernels initialize under memory pressure.
oncall-sre: immediate mitigation proposal:
- Pause autoscaler (manual suspend) to stop oscillation
- Evict non-critical low-priority jobs from GPU pool
- Roll pods to rdx-2b-quant only (fallback smaller model) for affected routes
- Increase pod eviction grace and kubelet reserved memory temporarily
sre_lead: agree. Do it in this order and coordinate with runtime-eng. @runtime-eng take lead on model fallback.
runtime-eng: starting canary routing to rdx-2b-quant now for high-traffic route /v1/chat-stream (will patch routing policy). Pushing config in 30s.
inc-bot: deploy-bot: started routing-change rollout by runtime-eng (change id: r-20260510-01).
runtime-eng: applied, canaries show reduced memory per pod (~30% lower). But still seeing a few OOMs during pod start.
oncall-sre: suspending autoscaler now: `kubectl patch deployment cluster-autoscaler -p '{"spec":{"paused":true}}'` — paused.
eng-platform: autoscaler paused. Noted: we still have elevated pod count; draining would help.
ops-shift: evicting best-effort workloads labeled low-priority-gpu across gpu-pool. Command: `kubectl delete pod -l low-priority-gpu -n batch-jobs --grace-period=30`.
prod-support: updating customer status: posting to status page that mitigating, partial brownout in eu-west, degraded responses for some models.
customer-success: flagged top-10 affected customers, offering runbooks and temporary quota increases for fallback endpoints.
ml-infra: investigating kernel/driver mismatch. Host dmesg shows multiple 'oom_kill_process' and 'NVRM: Xid 79' (GPU page fault) entries around same time.
runtime-eng: quick patch: increase kubelet --eviction-hard memory.available to 300Mi and reserved to 2Gi on nodes in pool. Rolling config via cloud-init; applying to 2 nodes first.
ops-shift: rolling kernel/driver restart on node gpu-node-az4-05 to clear stale allocations. Draining first: `kubectl drain gpu-node-az4-05 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`.
oncall-sre: note: draining will temporarily reduce capacity; ensure we keep enough pods. We're holding 6 spare pods in other regions.
eng-platform: set routing fallback to other region (us-central) for high-SLA tenants; will throttle eu-west new sessions.
prod-support: customers report improvement after fallback but some high-throughput customers still see elevated latency.
sre_lead: root cause hypothesis: autoscaler reacts to short spikes, overprovisioning nodes; nodes warm up slowly under kernel/driver version, memory fragmentation leads to OOMs when many pods initialize simultaneously -> crashloops -> autoscaler sees failing pods and keeps flipping desired count.
runtime-eng: long-term mitigations proposed:
- Add stabilization window to autoscaler (increase scale-down delay to 10m, require sustained lower metric)
- Add startup probes with staggered init to reduce concurrent allocations
- Harden model runtime to reserve a small persistent cache instead of preallocating everything
- Add driver compatibility checks on node join
eng-platform: I'll open an RFC for autoscale stabilization and a runbook entry for driver verification on node join.
ops-shift: nodes recovering after restart, new pods come up with lower peak mem. Monitoring closely.
inc-bot: PagerDuty: incident acknowledged by oncall-sre and runtime-eng. Severity: SEV2 -> reduced to SEV3 as errors drop.
oncall-sre: last 10m error rate: 5xx from 18% -> 3% after routing fallback and autoscaler pause. Latency p95 improved from 2.4s -> 1.1s for fallback route.
prod-support: leaving a note for customers about ETA: additional stabilization config changes scheduled in 2 hours. Offering post-incident review.
customer-success: creating follow-up ticket for affected accounts and scheduling deep-dive with runtime-eng.
sre_lead: action items assigned:
- eng-platform: RFC for autoscaler stabilizers (due 2026-05-17)
- runtime-eng: implement staggered startup probe patch (PR + canary, due 2026-05-14)
- ml-infra: validate quant profiles and driver compatibility across recent nodes (due 2026-05-12)
- ops-shift: add driver preflight on node bootstrap (due 2026-05-13)
- prod-support/customer-success: customer comms and credits follow-up (ongoing)
runtime-eng: leaving note: if we see repeat in other regions, we'll roll a hotfix to model runner to pre-check GPU free memory before allocation and fall back to swapped execution path.
oncall-sre: closing pager for now; monitoring 30m before full closure. Thanks all for quick coordination :thumbsup:
eng-platform: logging incident postmortem template entry and will kick off postmortem doc in #postmortems.
prod-support: will update status page once we confirm 30m window clean.
inc-bot: INCIDENT 1872003456 status: monitoring -> resolved (partial mitigations remain).
